comparison: Strong agreement on the core finding. Both evaluations find compelling evidence that recurrent feedback from SOM neurons can disentangle gain and stability control (C1-C3, C31-C33). OpenEval emphasizes the mathematical framework and internal consistency, while peer reviewers highlight the convincing nature of the evidence across all three reviewers. The claim about inverse relationship in feedforward circuits (C31-C32) and its resolution through feedback (C33) is accepted by both.

Disagreement on plasticity-related claims (C55-C61). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN because C61 is explicitly speculative and the manuscript does not model plasticity dynamics, noting the connection to plasticity mechanisms remains hypothetical. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as reasonable discussion points with appropriate citations and qualifications. The difference reflects OpenEval's stricter standard for speculative extensions versus peer acceptance of appropriately qualified implications.

Strong agreement on methodological approach (C20, C25, C27-C28, C67). Both evaluations endorse the linearization framework and its validation through noisy simulations. OpenEval notes the mathematical soundness and appropriate application of dynamical systems definitions. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the simplified mathematical model and the addition of simulations to extend beyond the linear range, with Reviewer 2 acknowledging the linearization limitation as appropriately addressed.

Agreement on rate-dependent effects (C29-C31). Both evaluations accept the modeling results showing rate-dependent heatmaps in Figure 3. OpenEval notes rigorous quantification through mathematical framework while acknowledging linearization limits. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the analytical framework praised by Reviewer 1, with Reviewer 2 highlighting the thorough investigation of connectivity effects.

Partial disagreement on reconciling experimental findings (C17-C19, C64-C65). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the modeling framework successfully reconciles contradictory experimental findings through mechanistic explanation (C21). Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 3's concern about lack of direct comparison to biological parameters and experiments, questioning how well the model explains diverse experimental observations despite not challenging the cited findings themselves.

Agreement on parameter sensitivity and connectivity effects (C40-C41, C53, C60). Both evaluations accept the modeling results showing complex dependencies on synaptic weights. OpenEval notes the claim about 'optimal' values requires careful interpretation. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight this thorough investigation as a major strength (Reviewer 2), providing opportunities to understand when gain and stability will or will not increase together.

Strong agreement on background and context claims (C4-C12, C13-C16, C22-C24, C34, C36, C45-C46, C51-C52). Both evaluations accept these literature-based claims as well-supported and accurate characterizations. OpenEval notes appropriate citations to historical and contemporary work. Peer reviewers do not challenge any background claims and note the intuitive summary statements are helpful, treating these as established knowledge.

Agreement on connectivity determining arithmetic of gain changes (C64-C66). Both evaluations accept the modeling demonstration in Figure 8. OpenEval notes the analysis extends beyond simple feedforward models. Peer reviewers include this as part of the thorough investigation of connectivity structure effects that Reviewer 2 identifies as a major strength, though the tuning analysis is acknowledged as more limited in scope.

Agreement on rate-dependent gain modulation (C43-C44). Both evaluations accept these findings. OpenEval notes the observation follows naturally from cellular gain terms in the mathematical framework. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the analytical findings, with Reviewer 1 noting convincing evidence from analytical calculations and numerical simulations.

Agreement on functional inferences about PV/SOM roles (C34-C37, C42, C50). Both evaluations accept these mechanistic inferences as reasonable interpretations. OpenEval notes consistency with modeling results while acknowledging the division is context-dependent. Peer reviewers accept these as reasonable interpretations, with Reviewer 2 noting excellent balance between biological detail and mathematical tractability, and Reviewer 3 acknowledging potentially interesting consequences for cortical computation.

Agreement on hypothesis framing and conceptual framework (C13-C16). Both evaluations accept these claims as appropriately framing the theoretical motivation. OpenEval notes C13 is explicitly labeled as hypothesis rather than established fact. Peer reviewers do not challenge these framing claims, treating them as part of the accepted scientific foundation.

Agreement on anatomical and definitional claims (C22-C24). Both evaluations accept these as establishing necessary biological context and definitions. OpenEval notes they are well-supported by citations to established literature. Peer reviewers do not challenge these claims, treating them as established knowledge.

Agreement on historical context (C62-C63). Both evaluations accept these claims as accurate characterizations of the literature evolution. OpenEval notes they set up the authors' contribution about circuit connectivity determining arithmetic properties. Peer reviewers accept these contextual claims without challenge as part of necessary background.

Agreement on methodological limitations and scope (C67-C68). Both evaluations accept these as appropriate acknowledgments. OpenEval notes the authors validate linearization with noisy simulations and discuss VIP neurons as future direction, showing scientific transparency. Peer reviewers endorse the methodological approach, with Reviewer 2 noting simulations verify findings hold in stochastically-driven regime.

Agreement on dendritic and plasticity background (C45-C50). Both evaluations accept these claims as supported by appropriate citations. OpenEval notes C50 is a conceptual extension rather than demonstrated result of current work. Peer reviewers accept these as part of well-supported background information, with no challenges raised.

Agreement on anatomical characterization and scope limitations (C51-C52). Both evaluations accept these claims about superficial layer connectivity and existing variations. OpenEval notes this represents appropriate scientific caution about generalizability. Peer reviewers do not challenge these claims, treating them as part of accepted background.
